items.title: Peter Vacher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001
items.q: there was a wonderful writer called Valerie Wilmer who is still very, very active. A number of us I think were starting out with the idea of interviewing as many visiting American musicians as we could get to.

ctx.x: Were you perhaps one of the first people to hit on some of these guys for stories do you think? Because nowadays a lot of them have been telling their stories a lot.

Well I can certainly recall, I mean I brought the book I wrote about Joe Darensbourg. That started, and that may be worth talking about for a minute or two, I saw his address in Leonard Feather’s own Encyclopedia of Jazz. So I wrote to him. You know, “Dear Joe, I’m an admirer of your music.” And we struck up a correspondence. He came to London in about 1962, just after I got married, with Louis Armstrong’s All-Stars. I interviewed him, that was the first time a full account of his career had ever appeared. That…

musicians as we could get to. Not necessarily the big stars, but sometimes the piano player and the bass player, rather than the top soloist perhaps. Because you’re right, obviously some of those have been interviewed extensively already. And I think that was quite a useful thing to do, enough of them was talking clearly for the first time in that sense. You know it was the first they’d been prompted to give their stories.
